12 mmHg).
2. Narrowed valve orifice impedes diastolic inflow from LA to LV , causing blood 
pooling in LA.
3. Ventricular diastole (when mitral valve is open).
4. Decreased LV filling reduces EDV , Stroke Volume, Cardiac Output, and 
systemic BP . Leads to pulmonary venous hypertension.
5. Mitral Stenosis.

1.End-Diastolic Volume (EDV): The total volume of blood in the ventricle at the end of diastole 
(filling phase), immediately prior to contraction (normally ~120 mL).
• End-Systolic Volume (ESV): The residual volume of blood remaining in the ventricle at the end of 
systole (ejection phase), after contraction completes (normally ~50 mL).
• Stroke Volume (SV): The volume of blood ejected from the ventricle during a single heartbeat, 
defined as SV = EDV - ESV (normally ~70 mL).
• Ejection Fraction (EF): The fraction of end-diastolic volume ejected with each stroke, serving as 
a key indicator of systolic pumping efficiency: EF = (SV / EDV) × 100% (normally ~58–60%).
• Cardiac Output (CO): The total volume of blood pumped by the ventricle per minute: CO = HR × 
SV (normally ~4900 mL/min or ~5.0 L/min).
2. Baseline Calculations (EDV = 120 mL, ESV = 50 mL, HR = 70 bpm):
• Stroke Volume (SV) = 120 mL - 50 mL = 70 mL
• Ejection Fraction (EF) = (70 mL / 120 mL) × 100% = 58.33%
• Cardiac Output (CO) = 70 beats/min × 70 mL = 4900 mL/min (4.9 L/min)
3. Pathological Evaluation (EDV = 120 mL, ESV = 80 mL):
• Recalculated SV = 120 mL - 80 mL = 40 mL
• Recalculated EF = (40 mL / 120 mL) × 100% = 33.33%
• Clinical Significance: A reduction in EF from 58% down to 33.3% signifies impaired myocardial 
contractility or severe afterload overload, characteristic of systolic heart failure. The ventricle 
fails to empty effectively, leaving an abnormally high residual end-systolic volume (80 mL vs. 50 
mL), which drastically reduces stroke volume and compromises systemic arterial perfusion.

1.CO = Heart Rate (HR) × Stroke Volume (SV). CO = 70 beats/min × 70 mL = 
4900 mL/min (~4.9–5.0 L/min). 
2. ESV remains unchanged (~50 mL); the heart ejects all the additional filling 
blood. 
3. The ventricle must spend more time generating higher pressure to open the 
aortic valve, reducing ejection time, decreasing stroke volume, and increasing 
ESV .
4. Answer: Sympathetic activation increases intracellular Ca²⁺ availability, 
accelerating cross-bridge cycling rate and force development.
5.Both preload and contractility increase during exercise, producing a larger PV 
loop with a significantly reduced End-Systolic Volume (ESV) due to vigorous 
ventricular emptying.
